userStories.title: Read and parse the review artifact
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add bounded review-artifact discovery and pure parsing without changing existing bundle partial semantics.

**Motivation** — The next PR then gets the same finding again.

**Approach** — Which artifact. The reader gains two slots: `nax-out/bot/pr-<n>/<runId>/bot-review.json` (`botReview`, may match more than one) and top-level `nax.stdout` (`naxStdout`). **Neither slot ever adds to the bundle's `oversized` list**: an oversized file in either slot is skipped silently, so a large `nax.stdout` on a `RUN` bundle never makes that ingest partial. The parser picks the `bot-review.json` whose path the stdout line `nax bot review: artifact <path>` names, matched on the path's trailing `bot/pr-<n>/<runId>/bot-review.json`. With no such line and exactly one `bot-review.json`, it uses that one; otherwise the artifact is `invalid` (reason `artifact-ambiguous`).

Artifact checks. The PR number comes from `prNumberOfReviewFeature(job.feature)`. The artifact must parse as JSON with `version` 1, 2 or 3, `pr.number` equal to that PR number, and a boolean `trusted`; otherwise it is `invalid` (reason `artifact-invalid`) and no rows are written. A missing `events` field means no events. Events whose `type` is not `finding-withdrawn` are ignored. A `finding-withdrawn` event needs string `key` (1..200 chars), `threadId` (1..200 chars), `finding`, `reason`, and a `disagreedBy` array of strings; an event missing one is dropped. `file` (string) and `line` (positive integer) are optional; a wrongly typed optional field is treated as absent. `finding` and `reason` are clipped to 1000 characters each. Logins that do not match `^[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9-]{0,38})(?:\[bot\])?$` are dropped, and `disagreedBy` keeps its first 10 valid logins. At most 50 events per artifact are kept (the first 50).

`BundleFiles` / `SLOTS` / `readBundleFiles`: Baseline: nine slots. Target: adds optional `botReview?: BundleFile[]` and `naxStdout?: BundleFile | null` per call 2. `parseBundle` gains an optional third parameter `opts: { reviewPrNumber?: number }`; when given, it returns `botReview` and records `files.botReview`, excluded from the partial calculation. Preserve path safety, existing slot behavior and existing callers.

**Scope** — In: reader slots, parser, additive parseBundle integration and unit tests in the existing reader/parse-bundle suites plus the new parser suite. Out: job eligibility, event persistence and post-commit emission (US-002); role checks/minting (US-003 through US-007). Turning agreed findings or any event type other than `finding-withdrawn` into memory. Checking `pr.repo` or `pr.forge` in the artifact against the job's repo; the job, its bundle and its PR number already tie the artifact to the repo.

**Interface** — `parseBotReview(files: BundleFiles, prNumber: number): BotReviewParse` where `BotReviewParse = { outcome: 'absent' } | { outcome: 'invalid'; reason: 'artifact-ambiguous' | 'artifact-invalid' } | { outcome: 'done'; trusted: boolean; events: WithdrawnEvent[] }` and `WithdrawnEvent = { key, threadId, file?, line?, finding, reason, disagreedBy }`.

userStories.title: Store review events at ingest
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist eligible review withdrawals atomically with bundle ingestion and notify minting only after commit.

**Motivation** — The next PR then gets the same finding again.

**Approach** — Two phases: store, then mint. The GitHub permission check is a network call, so it never runs inside the ingest transaction. The ingest stores each withdrawal as a `FleetReviewEvent` row in the same transaction as the rest of the bundle; after commit it emits `REVIEW_EVENTS_INGESTED`. A system writer, `ReviewEventMinter`, then checks permissions and mints decisions for `pending` rows. The row is also the record of every skipped event and its reason.

When the ingest reads it. Only for a `REVIEW` job whose state is `COMPLETED` at ingest time **and** whose `leaseEpoch` equals the claim's epoch. The outcome joins the ingest's per-file outcomes as `botReview`: `done`, `invalid` or `absent`. `botReview` never makes the ingest partial.

Untrusted PRs never mint (user ruling). When `trusted` is false, every event's row is written with status `skipped`, reason `untrusted-pr`.

Idempotent rows. `FleetReviewEvent` is unique on `(jobId, leaseEpoch, threadId)`; a re-ingest of the same bundle inserts nothing new (insert skipping duplicates) and never changes an existing row.

New `FleetReviewEvent` model + migration `20261115090000_fleet_review_event`: `id`, `jobId` (FK FleetJob, cascade), `leaseEpoch`, `projectId`, `repoId`, `prNumber`, `findingKey`, `threadId`, `file?`, `line?`, `finding`, `reason`, `disagreedBy String[]`, `trusted Boolean`, `status` (`pending` | `minted` | `skipped`), `skipReason?`, `approverLogin?`, `memoryItemId?`, `attempts Int @default(0)`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`; unique `(jobId, leaseEpoch, threadId)`; index `(status, createdAt)`.

`BundleIngestService`: Baseline: constructor ends with `private readonly audit: AuditRecorder`. Target: adds a last parameter `private readonly reviewEvents: FleetReviewEventsService`; `write` calls `recordForJob` inside the transaction per call 4; after commit emits `REVIEW_EVENTS_INGESTED` (`{ jobId }`, constant in `apps/api/src/fleet/common/review-events.ts`) when `pending > 0`. `IngestModule` imports `FleetReviewsModule`; `FleetReviewsModule` exports `FleetReviewEventsService` (its header comment stops saying it exports nothing).

Run `bun run db:generate` in `apps/api` after the schema edit; the Prisma client is git-ignored. Keep the repository module-private under `FLEET_REVIEW_EVENT_REPOSITORY`. claimPending is a pure read, oldest createdAt first; marks and attempt mutation are designed for bookkeeping wrappers added by US-006. Adjust positional constructor calls in bundle-ingest.service.spec.ts, bundle-ingest.outcomes.spec.ts, bundle-ingest.workflow.spec.ts and bundle-ingest.pr-links.spec.ts with a trailing `{ recordForJob: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ pending: 0 }) } as never`; every existing assertion is unchanged. Add this story's ingest unit tests to bundle-ingest.service.spec.ts. Preserve existing RUN rows, corrections and KNOWLEDGE_RUN_INGESTED hooks.

**Scope** — In: schema/migration, event repository/service, eligibility, same-transaction recording, post-commit event and real-Postgres ingest tests through drain/upload/requeue. Out: GitHub calls (US-003/US-006), memory minting (US-005/US-006), minter subscription/poller (US-007). Expiring or pruning `FleetReviewEvent` rows; they cascade with their job.

**Interface** — `recordForJob(job, leaseEpoch, parse): Promise<{ pending: number }>` (`pending` = rows this call newly inserted with status `pending`), `claimPending(limit)`, `markMinted(id, { memoryItemId, approverLogin })`, `markSkipped(id, reason)`, `bumpAttempt(id): Promise<number>` (returns the new count).

userStories.title: Ask GitHub for a login's role on a repo
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose a fail-closed GitHub repository permission query through the existing forge HTTP client.

**Motivation** — The next PR then gets the same finding again.

**Approach** — `GitHubAppClient` gains `getRepoRole(token, owner, name, login): Promise<'admin' | 'maintain' | 'write' | 'triage' | 'read' | 'none'>`: `GET /repos/{owner}/{name}/collaborators/{login}/permission`; 200 returns `role_name` when it is one of those values, else maps `permission` (`admin`, `write`, `read` map to themselves, anything else to `none`); 404 returns `none`; any other status throws `RepoCheckException('provider_error')`. The login is URL-encoded.

Use the existing `http.request` / `obj` / `repoPath` helpers and token headers; forge HTTP stays behind FleetHttpClient timeout/no-redirect policy, with no token logging or persistence. `apps/api/src/fleet/git-broker/github-app-client.spec.ts` adds tests for this story's acceptance criteria; every existing assertion is unchanged.

**Scope** — In: getRepoRole and fake-HTTP boundary tests. Out: minter orchestration that selects an approver, obtains tokens for pending rows and retries failures (US-006), audit approver types (US-004). GitLab reviews; K1 reviews GitHub repos only.

**Interface** — `getRepoRole(token, owner, name, login): Promise<'admin' | 'maintain' | 'write' | 'triage' | 'read' | 'none'>`.

userStories.title: Record a forge user as the approver
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry a forge identity as approval metadata while preserving the separate system actor and existing audit context.

**Motivation** — There is also no way to take a decision back: memory has no retire or supersede route (`memory.controller.ts` serves `extract`, `decisions` and create only).

**Approach** — Forge approver type. `ActionApproval.approverType` widens from `ActorType` to `ActorType | 'FORGE_USER'`, and so does `AuditEntryRecord.approverType`. The audit entry DTO's `approval.approverType` TypeScript union gains `FORGE_USER` (the OpenAPI schema is `type: Object` and does not change), and the audit display labels a `FORGE_USER` approver with its id (`github:alice`).

New `runWithApproval(approval: ActionApproval, fn)` in `action-context.ts`: runs `fn` in a copy of the current context with `approval` replaced; throws `Error('no action context')` outside one.

Update `ActionApproval.approverType`, `AuditEntryRecord.approverType`, `AuditEntryDto.approval.approverType` and `principalLabel` / `collectDisplayIds`. Keep FORGE_USER out of user/agent/runner identity lookup batches; do not widen actors or onBehalfOf principals and do not add a GitHub-login-to-user map. Existing optionality/nullability is preserved. Prisma already stores approverType as a string; no database or OpenAPI schema migration is needed. Extend existing recorder/log suites and add the run-with-approval suite, verifying nested async context restoration.

**Scope** — In: approval type widening, context helper, recorder propagation and literal forge display labels. Out: system-key declaration and decision audit hook (US-005), permission verification/approval selection (US-006), retirement (US-008). Mapping a GitHub login to a koda user; the approver is recorded as `FORGE_USER` / `github:<login>` only.

**Interface** — `runWithApproval(approval: ActionApproval, fn)`; `ActionApproval.approverType` is `ActorType | 'FORGE_USER'`.

userStories.title: Write a review decision and declare its system key
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the project-scoped review decision writer, durable duplicate/retirement guards and its auditable system-key declarer.

**Motivation** — The next PR then gets the same finding again.

**Approach** — The decision row (design D5). `kind DECISION`, `subject repo:<repoId>`, `predicate review-finding:<findingKey>`, `object` = `Not a defect: <finding>. Reason: <reason>` plus ` (<file>:<line>)` when both are present (` (<file>)` when only `file` is), `confidence 1.0`, `ownerId`/`ownerType` null, `sourceType review_event`, `sourceId <jobId>:<threadId>`. Written through `PrismaMemoryItemRepository.upsert`, so a newer withdrawal of the same finding key on the same repo supersedes the older one.

Mint guards, before any network call, in this order. `ReviewDecisionWriter.guard(input)` returns `{ status: 'skipped', reason: 'duplicate' }` when a `MemoryItem` with `sourceType review_event` and the same `sourceId` exists in any status; `{ status: 'skipped', reason: 'retired' }` when a `rejected` row with `sourceType review_event` and the same project, `subject` and `predicate` exists; otherwise `null`. `mint` runs the same guards again inside its write; when `mint` returns `{ status: 'skipped', reason }`, the minter calls `markSkipped(reason)`. A crash between `mint` and `markMinted` leaves the row `pending`; the next pass then ends it `skipped` / `duplicate` (the decision exists; the row's approver login is lost, the audit entry keeps it).

Audit. One `system.review.decision` entry per minted decision, actor `SYSTEM/review` (the design said `review-ingest`; the system actor id must be the key's second segment, `review`), approval `{ requiredMode: 'human', satisfiedBy: 'human', approverType: 'FORGE_USER', approverId: 'github:<login>' }` set with `runWithApproval` around `mint`, resource `memory-item` / the new id, summary `review decision from job <jobId>, PR #<prNumber>, approver github:<login> (one of the thread's commenters)`, written by the writer's own `onWritten` hook (not `memoryAuditHook`, whose summary is fixed).

`ReviewDecisionWriter` is provided and exported by `MemoryModule`; `reviewDecisionObject(input)` builds the call-8 `object`. `FleetReviewsModule` imports `MemoryModule`. `MemoryAuditKey` gains `system.review.decision`. Declare a `@SystemWriter('system.review.decision') ReviewEventMinter` class provided by FleetReviewsModule whose `run(): Promise<void>` resolves without doing anything in this story. Add `'system.review.decision': ['system']` immediately after `'system.pr-review.dispatch'` in the catalog in this same story, because undeclared catalog keys fail contracts. Pin the writer map with `[ReviewEventMinter, 'system.review.decision']` and exact count 35 -> 36. Role-matrix exact catalog cell count 221 -> 222; every role gains system.review.decision immediately after system.pr-review.dispatch with identical cells to that adjacent key; every other entry stays identical. Add one system inventory TSV row mirroring FleetPrReviewPass except the class/key and entry description for run on REVIEW_EVENTS_INGESTED and ReviewEventMintPoller setInterval. Integration ACs run mint inside `runAsSystem('review', ...)`; use runWithApproval where forge approval is asserted and real Postgres to verify memory/audit atomicity.

**Scope** — In: writer/object builder/guards, atomic custom audit hook, MemoryModule export/Reviews import, inert minter declarer, system catalog/role-matrix/writer-map/inventory pins. Out: event rows (US-002), the minter's orchestration and permission lookup (US-006), concurrency/event/timer lifecycle (US-007), retire key and route (US-008). Passing decisions into the review and the decisions selection; those are part A (feature `fleet-review-decisions`). This feature defines its own `review_event` and `repo:<id>` literals and does not import part A's module.

**Interface** — `ReviewDecisionInput = { projectId, repoId, prNumber, jobId, threadId, findingKey, finding, reason, file?, line? }`; `ReviewDecisionWriter.guard(input)`; `ReviewDecisionWriter.mint(input): Promise<{ status: 'minted'; memoryItemId: string } | { status: 'skipped'; reason: 'duplicate' | 'retired' }>`; `reviewDecisionObject(input)`; `ReviewEventMinter.run(): Promise<void>`.

userStories.title: Mint pending review events
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Turn pending trusted withdrawals into decisions only after a verified repository writer is found, with durable skip and retry outcomes.

**Motivation** — The next PR then gets the same finding again.

**Approach** — Approver = a writer. For a `pending` row, in this order: drop logins that end in `[bot]` from `disagreedBy` (none left: `skipped`, reason `no-writer`, before any lookup); run the call-9 guards; load the repo with `FleetReposService.findReviewRepo` (missing repo, or no `githubInstallationId`: `skipped`, reason `repo-unavailable`); mint a read-only token (`mintReadOnlyToken`); then walk the remaining logins in order, asking `getRepoRole` for each. The first login whose role is `admin`, `maintain` or `write` is the approver. No such login: `skipped`, reason `no-writer`. A `getRepoRole` that throws: `skipped`, reason `permission-check-failed` (never minted on an unverified login).

Mint guards, before any network call, in this order. `ReviewDecisionWriter.guard(input)` returns `{ status: 'skipped', reason: 'duplicate' }` when a `MemoryItem` with `sourceType review_event` and the same `sourceId` exists in any status; `{ status: 'skipped', reason: 'retired' }` when a `rejected` row with `sourceType review_event` and the same project, `subject` and `predicate` exists; otherwise `null`. `mint` runs the same guards again inside its write; when `mint` returns `{ status: 'skipped', reason }`, the minter calls `markSkipped(reason)`. A crash between `mint` and `markMinted` leaves the row `pending`; the next pass then ends it `skipped` / `duplicate` (the decision exists; the row's approver login is lost, the audit entry keeps it).

Read the API and CLI authoring contexts. The detected Express/Next.js labels in the prompt are not authoritative: apps/api is NestJS 12 on Fastify, with Express-compatible HTTP test helpers, Prisma 7/Postgres and Vitest; the web is Nuxt and needs no changes. API owns persistence, permissions, approval, audit and business rules; CLI stays a generated-client consumer. No runner, web or nax transport changes are required. The binding spec has exactly eleven stories, with its specified dependency graph and package workdirs even where a story also updates root contract/inventory artifacts. The original combined K2 design still says DRAFT (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-31-fleet-s6-k2-review-memory-design.md:3); the approved, later feature spec and its ACs govern this implementation, not that stale status or part-A requirements.

Existing ingest seam: BundleFiles has nine slots, with featureReport/decisions optional to preserve old literal fixtures (apps/api/src/fleet/ingest/bundle-reader.ts:10-37). slotOf rejects absolute paths, backslashes and traversal before matching the allowlist (:40-46); keep that security boundary. readBundleFiles streams tar.gz, keeps regular files only, and currently adds every oversized allowlisted file to oversized (:64-101). botReview and naxStdout must be exceptions to that oversized accounting, not a global weakening of limits. Multiple review artifacts are retained for stdout-tail disambiguation; stdout is selection data, never an instruction or a path to read from disk. parseBundle is pure, currently takes two arguments, accumulates per-file outcomes and excludes workflow invalidity from partial (apps/api/src/fleet/ingest/parse-bundle.ts:28-68). Extend it additively with optional reviewPrNumber and optional botReview result, preserving existing RUN outcome behavior and all prior callers. The workflow parser demonstrates typed readers, clipped strings and bounded arrays (apps/api/src/fleet/ingest/parsers/workflow.parser.ts:1-42). PR identity is recoverable only from the existing safe-integer parser of review-pr-<n> (apps/api/src/fleet/common/review-jobs.ts:7-12). Never infer a different PR from artifact content.

BundleIngestService already locks the job and executes parsing, replaceRows, corrections, outcome and audit inside txManager.run, then publishes live/budget/ticket/knowledge effects after commit (apps/api/src/fleet/ingest/bundle-ingest.service.ts:93-133). ingestOne catches read/write failures and records retry/failure (:76-90, :136-150). Record FleetReviewEvent rows atomically with the ingest, only for command REVIEW, state COMPLETED at the locked read, and the same claim epoch. Do not interfere with RUN-only outcome storage (:100-105) or its KNOWLEDGE_RUN_INGESTED event (:126-133). review pending count must travel in the transaction result so REVIEW_EVENTS_INGESTED cannot escape a rollback. The row write is insert-with-duplicate-skip, unlike replaceRows; requeue must never reset attempts, status, timestamps or historical reviewer data. Add the final reviewEvents constructor collaborator and adjust the four positional-constructor suites: bundle-ingest.service.spec.ts:17,132; bundle-ingest.outcomes.spec.ts:32,92; bundle-ingest.workflow.spec.ts:47,121; bundle-ingest.pr-links.spec.ts:25. One existing service fixture at :17 currently omits the audit argument too: retain/restore the existing audit stub position before appending reviewEvents rather than shifting arguments or weakening assertions. IngestModule currently imports no Reviews module and explicitly avoids KnowledgeModule (apps/api/src/fleet/ingest/ingest.module.ts:18-32); add FleetReviewsModule only.

Persistence/module design: FleetReviewsModule currently imports FleetReposModule, FleetJobsModule, GitBrokerModule and exports nothing (apps/api/src/fleet/reviews/fleet-reviews.module.ts:12-30). Add the private FLEET_REVIEW_EVENT_REPOSITORY binding, exported FleetReviewEventsService, MemoryModule, minter and poller in their assigned stories; update the misleading header. Existing PrismaFleetPrReviewRepository uses transaction-scoped PrismaService.client via ALS (apps/api/src/fleet/reviews/prisma-fleet-pr-review.repository.ts:12-28); follow that repository pattern without copying its mutating claim semantics: claimPending here is a pure ordered read, not a lease, status change or SKIP LOCKED claim. Migration 20261115090000_fleet_review_event must create the full model, job cascade FK, unique (jobId, leaseEpoch, threadId), index (status, createdAt), default attempts 0 and timestamps. Add the FleetJob backrelation. Use strings/local types for statuses, no Prisma enums. Run bun run db:generate in apps/api after schema edits; generated Prisma code is ignored. Persist skipped rows too, particularly untrusted-pr. Bookkeeping marks/attempt bumps use the new exact fleet.review-event-bookkeeping reason, while recordForJob remains part of counted ingest writes. claimPending reads at most twenty pending rows oldest first, single-flight is process-local, and the architecture assumes one API instance; do not silently add a distributed queue or claim mutation. Integration fixtures at apps/api/test/integration/fleet/fleet-pr-review.integration.spec.ts:12-50 demonstrate canRunDbTests, bootHttpApp, fixtureDb and action context wrappers.

Forge and trust boundary: GitHubAppClient centralizes FleetHttpClient requests, bearer headers, URL helpers and provider errors (apps/api/src/fleet/git-broker/github-app-client.ts:46-100, :128-180). mintReadOnlyToken already returns { token, expiresAt } with contents+metadata read (:74-78). getRepoRole must reuse the HTTP client, encode the login as one segment, trust only the six enumerated role_name values, fall back only to admin/write/read permission values, treat 404 as none and every other non-200 as provider_error. Do not broaden token scope, log tokens, or perform forge calls inside a DB transaction. A real GitHub deployment may deny the collaborator endpoint with the existing App permissions: the specified result is permission-check-failed and no mint, not insecure fallback. FleetReposService currently delegates internal reads through its repo, including listAutoReviewRepos (apps/api/src/fleet/repos/fleet-repos.service.ts:28-39, :109-111); add a narrow findReviewRepo projection using the existing findById seam. Do not make a public principal route or duplicate forge access checks there. Filter [bot] logins before any lookup, then duplicate/retired guards before repo/token/role network work. The first verified admin/maintain/write login wins in original order; a role lookup exception is a terminal permission-check-failed skip, whereas token mint or decision mint errors retry only three times. Untrusted PRs never reach minting. disagreedBy means all thread commenters, not a proven vote; audit must not overclaim consensus.

Action context/audit seam: ActionApproval currently accepts only ActorType USER|AGENT (apps/api/src/action-context/action-context.ts:24, :41-48); widen only the approver field, not actors, onBehalfOf, principals or permission identity. runWithActionContext uses AsyncLocalStorage and copies the input with shared correlation (:89-107); runWithApproval must nest a copy, preserve actor/onBehalfOf/origin/correlationId, restore on return or asynchronous settlement and throw outside a context. runAsSystemWriter derives the system actor from the second segment of its declared key (:141-151), so system.review.decision means SYSTEM/review, never review-ingest. AuditEntryRecord.approverType is currently ActorType|null (apps/api/src/audit/domain/audit-entry.domain.ts:8-27), and the DTO approval block has a TypeScript union but Swagger type Object (apps/api/src/audit/dto/audit-entry.dto.ts:13-20); no audit OpenAPI schema expansion is intended. collectDisplayIds and principalLabel currently batch users/agents/runners and return null for other types (apps/api/src/audit/audit-log.service.ts:35-71); FORGE_USER must bypass identity-table lookup and display its id literally. Prisma AuditEntry already stores approverType as String? (apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:857-870), so this widening needs no schema migration.

Memory writer/replacement seam: MemoryItem already has project-scoped active-key uniqueness and a source lookup index; rejected rows clear activeKey and remain history (apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:640-670). PrismaMemoryItemRepository.upsert runs a Serializable transaction, looks up the active key, handles replay no-op, optionally checks beforeSupersede, supersedes and inserts, then awaits onWritten inside the write transaction (apps/api/src/memory/prisma-memory-item.repository.ts:182-267). ReviewDecisionWriter must use that API, but first and again inside its write check sourceType review_event+sourceId across any status, then rejected review_event by project/subject/predicate; an active-only or non-project-scoped lookup would violate crash safety or isolation. Keep guards and memory+audit writes atomic; validate transaction nesting with the repository's existing ALS behavior rather than using an untracked root Prisma client. In a crash after mint but before event marking, a later guard produces duplicate, not a recreated item; audit remains the authoritative approver record. memoryAuditHook has a fixed created/superseded summary (apps/api/src/memory/memory-audit.ts:11-46), so use the review writer's own onWritten hook for the exact job/PR/forge approver summary and add its audit-key union member. Preserve supersession through upsert for a newer job/thread with the same project/repo/finding key. A rejected review finding is a durable veto against recreation, unlike superseded history. Part A is not a dependency: define review_event and repo:<id> locally.

Permissions/contracts are deliberately exact: PERMISSION_CATALOG places memory.decision.record at apps/api/src/permissions/catalog.ts:256 and system.pr-review.dispatch at :344. Retirement is an access-control change: MemoryWriteService currently checks project membership before keys, applies ownership on replacement and blocks generic DECISION creation (apps/api/src/memory/memory-write.service.ts:47-59, :83-104, :194-202). MemoryWriteGuard.mayReplace passes typed ownership as the resource for memory.update; null/partial ownership cannot satisfy .own (apps/api/src/memory/memory-write.guard.ts:49-74, :82-94). Reuse it inside retirement's transaction, not only as an HTTP precheck. retireTarget resolves a live item and membership first, hides any membership refusal as 404, then checks DECISION before active status; this resolution precedes approval gating so callers cannot probe foreign project metadata. retireDecision rechecks state/kind and permission at execution, atomically rejects, clears activeKey and records the reason-bearing audit. Existing repository.reject (apps/api/src/memory/prisma-memory-item.repository.ts:293-298) is only a low-level mutation; calling it alone would miss transactional rechecks and audit. MemoryController uses ApprovalRouteGate and ApprovalPending/JsonResponse (apps/api/src/memory/memory.controller.ts:24-69). MemoryRouteCommands registers durable replay parsers with ActorPrincipalLoader (apps/api/src/memory/memory-route.commands.ts:19-56); register the new rest:memory.decision.retire variant so deferred approvals execute the same service. A 202 must leave memory unchanged; a later stale execution must settle the approval failed/execution-failed, not report success. Default immediate POST success is 201, not 200. Add bilingual memory messages and the 422 custom exception matching apps/api/src/fleet/repos/auto-review.exception.ts:3-7.

Migration/rollout: developer currently names memory.decision.record in apps/api/src/permissions/system-roles.ts:56-94 and is an unlocked stored system role. US-009 ships the idempotent JSONB permissions data migration 20261116090000_developer_memory_decision_retire that inserts only into developer after record when missing, retaining order, custom entries and all other roles. Use the SQL/data-test precedent apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261111090000_retire_fleet_approval_keys/migration.sql:1-15 and developer-bash-decide-migration.integration.spec.ts. No deletion or expiry of review-event history beyond job cascade. Retired memory vetoes remain after job deletion because they are memory history.

Module/timer risks: FleetPrReviewPass shows @SystemWriter/runAsSystemWriter (apps/api/src/fleet/reviews/fleet-pr-review.pass.ts:33-62), while the existing poller owns single-flight and also checks prReviewEnabled (apps/api/src/fleet/reviews/fleet-pr-review.poller.ts:19-39). This feature intentionally differs: ReviewEventMinter.run itself owns single-flight and never rejects, covering event and timer entry together, and its timer is gated by sweepEnabled only. Add reviewMintPollMs to the IFleetConfig interface/schema/factory and the complete fleet-config test literal, using FLEET_REVIEW_MINT_POLL_MS and default 300000 (existing related config at apps/api/src/config/fleet.config.ts:68,107,133-170). A full page or overlapping event wake is allowed to wait for the next poll; do not add recursion, indefinite draining or transactions around HTTP. MemoryModule already has real forwardRef cycles through Projects/Agents/Context and exports the repository and write guard (apps/api/src/memory/memory.module.ts:27-65). Preserve those existing edges when adding writer/tools exports and importing MemoryModule in Reviews. Both FleetReviewsModule and IngestModule have no-DB DI tests (apps/api/src/fleet/reviews/fleet-reviews.module.spec.ts:25-59; apps/api/src/fleet/ingest/ingest.module.spec.ts:14-32), and MemoryModule has its own (:20-56). Extend those unit suites rather than putting compilation tests behind Postgres.

MCP seam: ApprovalMcpTools.registrations universally lists direct approval tools and establishes AGENT/mcp action context before service calls (apps/api/src/approvals/mcp/approval-mcp-tools.ts:18-85). MemoryMcpTools should likewise be universally visible, validate unknown keys and reason length, call retireTarget and the same route gate, and translate done/pending/errors into MCP text without bypassing permissions. McpController appends approval tools after permission-filtered assistant tools (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/mcp/mcp.controller.ts:50-70); append memory tools after those, inject the new collaborator and add its stub to the route-unit test. The real ApprovalRouteGate/ApprovalGate currently returns status executed for an immediate write, not done (apps/api/src/approvals/route/approval-route-gate.ts:55-90; apps/api/src/approvals/approval-gate.service.ts:20-21,111). Preserve the explicit spec unit AC for a gate stub returning done while also interoperating with the real executed outcome; do not change the shared gate contract. The existing AssistantModule already imports MemoryModule, so avoid a redundant module edge. Preserve all exact MCP tool lists and approval-tools relative order while appending one new final tool.

CLI seam and generated artifacts: apps/cli/src/commands/memory.ts:1-21 imports generated functions and resolves slugs only for project-ID writes; :68-109 shows existing success/JSON/handleApiError conventions. Retire identifies its project server-side from id, so bootstrap the API client with withContext({}, { requireProject: false }) instead of forcing local project context or resolving a slug (apps/cli/src/utils/context.ts:5-50). Add memoryControllerRetireDecision to the generated-boundary mocks, not handwritten HTTP. apps/cli/src/commands/memory.spec.ts:15-59 uses Jest, Commander parseAsync and mocked process.exit/console; preserve all existing assertions. Root package.json:19-23 defines bun run generate as API export plus CLI generation. Despite general prose claiming generated CLI files are committed, actual .gitignore:21-26 ignores apps/cli/src/generated and Prisma generated output; regenerate rather than hand-edit and commit tracked openapi.json only. US-008 must generate the new operation/RetireDecisionDto for US-011; no unrelated OpenAPI changes and no audit schema expansion.

Verification built into every story: API unit tests use vi and no DB; CLI uses Jest and mocks generated functions. PG tests belong in test/integration and use canRunDbTests; module/DI tests remain src/*.spec.ts with GlobalStubsModule. KODA_DB_TESTS=1 outside NAX_SANDBOXED=1 is required for genuine PG evidence. Run scoped DB specs on the host; skipping in a sandbox is not verification. DB-mode runs force-reset a *_test DB; never run parallel DB suites against the same database, and a second worktree uses KODA_TEST_DB_CONTAINER=1. Acceptance artifacts are generated under apps/<app>/.nax/features/fleet-review-ingest, are not story-authored outputs and must not be edited or copied. Keep the API Vitest SWC/decorator path, generated-client regeneration and exact contract pins intact. Security-sensitive role lookup, identity/approval attribution, system-key declaration, minter authorization, retirement gates/migrations and MCP all use strict three-session-tdd. Parsing, thin CLI formatting and the standard event/timer lifecycle use tdd-simple. The refine audit reduced approval metadata, timer wiring, stored-role rollout and direct MCP tool work to medium complexity because they reuse existing patterns; the retire route is complex rather than expert. Security-sensitive stories retain three-session-tdd regardless of reduced complexity. Refine audit enumerated all 117 explicit spec ACs by story ordinal: US-001 1-15, US-002 1-14, US-003 1-8, US-004 1-7, US-005 1-13, US-006 1-15, US-007 1-8, US-008 1-15, US-009 1-10, US-010 1-7 and US-011 1-5. Every story already has a negative-path AC; none needed an invented failure condition. Explicit failure-table cases lacking standalone ACs are enumerated in the appropriate story. The refine request additionally requires backward-compatibility assertions; seven were added for two-argument parseBundle, existing RUN outcome forwarding, unchanged token scope, independent PR-review config defaults, existing durable memory.create execution, the pre-existing MCP tool prefix and CLI decision self-attribution. Other optional hardening remains in suggestedCriteria. outOfScope: Mapping a GitHub login to a koda user; the approver is recorded as `FORGE_USER` / `github:<login>` only.
Turning agreed findings or any event type other than `finding-withdrawn` into memory.
GitLab reviews; K1 reviews GitHub repos only.
Re-checking a `skipped` event later (for example after a GitHub outage); a `skipped` row stays skipped.

Classifying each comment in a withdrawn thread as agreement or disagreement; nax's withdrawal is taken as the judgment, and `disagreedBy` is used only to pick a writer, so the recorded approver may be any writer who commented in the thread.
A web UI for review events or for retiring decisions; the audit page shows the new entries.
Retiring memory items of kinds other than `DECISION`, and un-retiring a decision.

Passing decisions into the review and the decisions selection; those are part A (feature `fleet-review-decisions`). This feature defines its own `review_event` and `repo:<id>` literals and does not import part A's module.
Expiring or pruning `FleetReviewEvent` rows; they cascade with their job.
Re-pinning the approver login on a row whose decision was minted just before a crash; the next pass ends that row `skipped` / `duplicate`, and the audit entry keeps the approver.
Checking `pr.repo` or `pr.forge` in the artifact against the job's repo; the job, its bundle and its PR number already tie the artifact to the repo.
